newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU and ACP states to discuss new Lome Convention.
newsitem.headline: EU and ACP states to discuss new Lome Convention.

text.p: The European Union and its main trading partners in the developing world meet in the southern Dutch town of Maastricht on Friday to work out the shape of their relations in the next century.

Political and economic ties between the EU and the 70 African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) states are enshrined in the Lome Convention, a 25-year-old framework for trade and aid that expires in the year 2000.
The Dutch government, as current EU President, says the convention needs to be amended "because of the essential changes which have taken place on the world stage in the last 10 years."
The two-day ministerial meeting will focus on the framework for financial cooperation before moving on Saturday to discussions on trade and economic cooperation.

One of the hottest trade issues will the European Union's banana regime, which has sparked a war of words between Brussels and Washington. The regime favours imports from mainly Caribbean countries but was recently found by a World Trade Organisation dispute panel to violate open trading rules.
In an interim ruling the WTO found in favour of a complaint by the United States and four Latin American countries that the EU regime dicriminated against their companies.
If a final WTO decision goes against the EU, Brussels may have to pay compensation to the United States, Ecuador, Mexico, Guatamala and Honduras for their lost export revenue.
Another issue at the top of some African countries' agenda will be the thorny issue of cocoa use in chocolate manufacture.

Cocoa producers, such as the Ivory Coast, want the European Union to ban the use of vegetable fat in chocolate. But manufacturers, particularly in Britain, want to maintain the current situation in which a five percent inclusion of non-cocoa material is allowed.
